scoreMeaning: An editorial craft judgment of the inspected local brand application: a coherent, appealing and honestly situated implementation with a useful personal-fit choice, held below exceptional because the smallest application weakens the signature gesture and the story remains a general question more than a specific authored observation. This is not a calibrated audience result, an overall motion score or evidence that the prior unscored brand became numerically better. A target of 9 has no role in this score.
strengths: The character has a subject now. What should software remember? and the persistent eva.md link connect the curious glance to a real project, so the scene asks something useful instead of merely advertising cuteness.

The investigation poses remain small and gentle. Glasses, a modest head turn and an open mitten are enough to express an invitation without changing the oversized head, compact body, paddle antennae, attached feet or layered wings.
The day and night paint sheets retain the same family. The quieter night treatment preserves an inviting cream face and identifiable antennae without making the moth into a glowing prop.

The project copy says exploring, not solved. The fetched README supports the mechanism and contains explicit live-verification limitations; the scene does not invent adoption, performance, an achievement or an anecdote.
The signature begins at a usable still; the question and destination stay available. The visible controls and inspected reduced-motion branch preserve a meaningful invitation when motion is absent.

Nag's explicit Investigate & share preference is relevant evidence for this being his personal identity. I support that as the lead local signature while keeping the wry and one-peek auditions labelled as studies.
The mobile studio's single-theme mode supplies a substantial character view. It is a meaningful improvement to inspection and ownership of the character, independent of any numerical test count.

workflowChanges: Separate review lanes for the character's expressive performance and frequently used study controls. The keyboard path should respond promptly; that does not forbid a keyboard user from explicitly playing a character film.
Require a stated purpose for each brand movement and check that the same useful project information survives in the still. The existing finite, user-triggered approach fits this rule.
Use same-context, actual-size comparisons for owner choice, especially on the phone. Contact-sheet thumbnails are supporting pose analysis, not a substitute for evaluating a full scene.
Record the choice axis: warm invitation versus a restrained afterthought. Keep personal fit and unfamiliar-viewer response separate, with evidence type attached to each claim.
Root is adding hover/coarse-pointer polish discovered through the installed skills; require fresh final-source evidence instead of quietly carrying an old review forward.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason: Prototype is explicit-invocation-only and a divergence/build workflow. This task asks to review installed workflow options and an existing implementation, so no new picker or prototype cleanup was triggered.

Prototype's default of three genuinely different directions is not a reason to manufacture another character direction: these are controlled performance auditions with a shared opening, and the user already selected a lead.
Prototype's delete-after-choice rule does not override the repository's explicit preservation of historical review studies and source evidence.
Emil's sub-300ms rule concerns UI feedback. The 4.1-second authored investigation is the subject being watched, not a delayed button or navigation response.
Emil's keyboard-no-animation wording is applied to control/navigation feedback, not to denying keyboard users access to an explicitly requested character performance.

A blanket transform/opacity-only rule would remove expressive SVG facial and hand rendering. This review cannot assert compositor performance from that heuristic; the appropriate performance evidence belongs to the technical review.
No reason to add stagger, spring bounce, blur, a tooltip, or Sonner solely because a skill describes it. The inspected scene already has a bounded purpose and stable content.
